Stop guessing at the wine list. Snap a photo and Sip Savvy picks bottles that match your taste and are fairly priced compared to retail.

HOW IT WORKS:

Scan Any Wine List Instantly – Take a photo of any menu, from bistros to Michelin-starred restaurants.

Get Smart Matches Based on Taste – See wines ranked by your preferences, expert reviews, and fair pricing.

Choose with Confidence Every Time – Our unique score shows your best option at a glance.

KEY FEATURES:

Personalized Recommendations – Start in seconds with Quick Profiles or build your own taste preferences.

See the Real Value – Instantly spot hidden gems and overpriced bottles with retail price comparisons.

Build Your Digital Wine Cellar – Save, track, and rate every wine you order to discover patterns in your taste.

One Trusted Score – Sip Savvy blends your profile, critic ratings, and pricing into a single confidence score.

Whether you’re exploring bold reds or crisp whites, Sip Savvy gives you the confidence of a sommelier in your pocket.

Download today and never stress over a wine list again!

quotes.text:
I really like wine, but my knowledge is not that extensive and in particular drops off pretty rapidly outside of California wines. Even within varietals and regions I’m familiar with, I don’t always know what characteristics to expect from a specific bottle - will this zin be peppery? Juicy? Etc.

I built an app to streamline this. You set what kind of wine you’re looking for and your price point, take a picture of the wine list, and it does the rest. It returns the menu ranked by:
- Alignment: How well it matches your flavor preferences.
- Value: The markup compared to retail price.
- Quality: Critics’ scores and online ratings.

It also provides a full description/tasting notes for each wine, which many wine lists leave out.

The Tech Stack

- Client: React Native

- Backend: FastAPI, deployed on Google Cloud Run

- DB: Firestore & Algolia

Here are the major pieces of the pipeline:

Image to Wine List: This is a combination of standard OCR and agentic image recognition. OCR alone couldn’t correctly parse layout (grouping prices with the right items), but "agentic alone" often hallucinated characters. I used Google Vision for the raw text and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite to structure it.

Matching (List → Database): Actually the hardest part. Wine lists take a lot of liberty with naming, and it’s tricky to know if a fuzzy match is close enough. I used Algolia here with custom ranking rules.
